title: Bitcoin Technical History
description: An interactive timeline of Bitcoin's technical evolution, featuring major soft forks, cryptographic breakthroughs, and active proposals based on Bitcoin Optech.
author: Gemini 3.1 Pro

nodes.label: Bitcoin Whitepaper
nodes.shortInfo: Satoshi Nakamoto publishes the Bitcoin whitepaper, describing a peer-to-peer electronic cash system.

sections.heading: The Beginning
sections.content: The original design of Bitcoin, introducing the blockchain, proof-of-work, and the UTXO model to solve the double-spending problem without a trusted third party.

nodes.label: nLockTime Enforcement
nodes.shortInfo: Hardcoded activation at block 31,000 to enforce nLockTime consensus rules.

sections.heading: First Soft Fork
sections.content: The earliest known soft fork in Bitcoin, implemented in version 0.1.6, activated via a hardcoded block height to enforce transaction locktimes.

nodes.label: P2SH (Pay-to-Script-Hash)
nodes.shortInfo: Allows transactions to be sent to a script hash, moving the burden of providing the conditions to the spender.

sections.heading: Standardizing Complex Scripts
sections.content: BIP16 introduced P2SH to simplify the use of complex scripts, like multisig, by allowing the sender to fund a 20-byte hash, leaving the spender to reveal the full script and signatures.

nodes.label: Duplicate TXID Fix
nodes.shortInfo: Prevents blocks from containing transactions with identical TXIDs to unspent outputs.

sections.heading: Security Fix
sections.content: Prevented an attack where duplicate transaction IDs could overwrite old UTXOs, inadvertently destroying user funds.

nodes.label: Coinbase Block Height
nodes.shortInfo: Requires coinbase transactions to include the block height, ensuring unique TXIDs.

sections.heading: Ensuring Unique Transactions
sections.content: Further mitigated the duplicate TXID issue by forcing coinbase transactions to include the block height, guaranteeing that every new coinbase transaction (and thus its TXID) is unique.

nodes.label: Strict DER Signatures
nodes.shortInfo: Requires all ECDSA signatures to be strictly DER-encoded.

sections.heading: Consensus Stability
sections.content: Resolved an issue where discrepancies in OpenSSL versions across different operating systems could lead to unintentional chain splits due to varying signature parsing rules.

nodes.label: OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY (CLTV)
nodes.shortInfo: Allows a transaction output to be made unspendable until a certain point in the future.

sections.heading: Absolute Timelocks
sections.content: Introduced OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, enabling trustless contract protocols, including Hash Time Locked Contracts (HTLCs), which are foundational for the Lightning Network.

nodes.label: Relative Timelocks (CSV)
nodes.shortInfo: Allows outputs to be timelocked relative to the confirmation time of their parent transaction.

sections.heading: Sequence Numbers and OP_CSV
sections.content: Repurposed the nSequence field for consensus-enforced relative locktimes and introduced OP_CHECKSEQUENCEVERIFY. This enabled bi-directional payment channels to remain open indefinitely.

nodes.label: Segregated Witness (Segwit)
nodes.shortInfo: Fixed transaction malleability and increased effective block size by separating signatures from transaction data.

sections.heading: Malleability Fix and Capacity Increase
sections.content: Segwit fixed the long-standing transaction malleability issue, making second-layer networks like Lightning safe to deploy. It also introduced block weight limits, effectively increasing on-chain capacity.

nodes.label: Taproot
nodes.shortInfo: Introduced Schnorr signatures, MAST, and Tapscript to improve privacy, efficiency, and scripting capabilities.

sections.heading: Schnorr and MAST
sections.content: Schnorr signatures allow for key and signature aggregation, making multisig indistinguishable from single-sig. MAST allows complex smart contracts to hide unexecuted branches, saving space and improving privacy.

nodes.label: Lightning Network
nodes.shortInfo: Layer-2 payment protocol utilizing payment channels for instant, low-fee microtransactions.

sections.heading: Scalable Off-Chain Payments
sections.content: Uses LN-Penalty, HTLCs, and onion routing to create a scalable, off-chain network of payment channels. Made viable by the malleability fix in Segwit.

nodes.label: Coinjoin
nodes.shortInfo: Trustless protocol for mixing UTXOs from multiple owners to obscure transaction history.

sections.heading: Privacy Enhancement
sections.content: Allows multiple participants to combine inputs and outputs into a single large transaction, breaking the heuristic that all inputs to a transaction belong to the same entity.

nodes.label: MuSig
nodes.shortInfo: A multi-signature scheme for Schnorr signatures allowing n-of-n signers to produce a single aggregated signature.

sections.heading: Scriptless Multisignatures
sections.content: Enabled by Taproot, MuSig allows multiple parties to aggregate their keys and signatures into one, saving block space and making multisig transactions look identical to single-sig.

nodes.label: PSBT
nodes.shortInfo: Partially Signed Bitcoin Transactions standardize the format for passing unsigned or partially signed transactions between software/hardware.

sections.heading: Interoperability
sections.content: Allows hardware wallets, air-gapped devices, and multi-sig coordinators to seamlessly exchange transaction data and signatures.

nodes.label: Discreet Log Contracts
nodes.shortInfo: Oracle-based smart contracts that hide the contract terms from the blockchain.

sections.heading: Private Oracle Contracts
sections.content: Parties agree to terms off-chain. An oracle later publishes a signature corresponding to the outcome, which the winning party uses to claim funds. The oracle doesn't need to know about the contract.

nodes.label: OP_CHECKTEMPLATEVERIFY (CTV)
nodes.shortInfo: A covenant proposal allowing an output to restrict the specific transaction structure that can spend it.

sections.heading: Covenants and Congestion Control
sections.content: CTV allows a transaction to commit to the outputs of the transaction that spends it. Use cases include congestion control, vault creation, and scaling solutions like Channel Factories and Timeout Trees.

nodes.label: SIGHASH_ANYPREVOUT (APO)
nodes.shortInfo: A signature hash type that does not commit to the specific UTXO being spent, enabling floating transactions.

sections.heading: Enabling Eltoo
sections.content: APO is necessary for the Eltoo (LN-Symmetry) protocol, an alternative to LN-Penalty that allows any later channel state to replace any earlier state without toxic waste.

nodes.label: OP_CAT
nodes.shortInfo: Proposal to restore a disabled opcode that concatenates two stack elements.

sections.heading: Versatile Scripting
sections.content: Originally disabled in 2010 due to memory exhaustion risks, safe variants are now proposed. It can emulate covenants, enable quantum-resistant signatures, and support complex off-chain protocols.

nodes.label: Package Relay
nodes.shortInfo: Allows nodes to relay groups of related transactions together, evaluating their combined feerate.

sections.heading: Fixing CPFP for 0-fee transactions
sections.content: Solves the issue where a parent transaction below the minimum relay fee cannot be broadcast, preventing child-pays-for-parent (CPFP) fee bumping. Critical for LN channel closures.

nodes.label: V3 Transaction Relay
nodes.shortInfo: A modified set of transaction relay policies designed to prevent transaction pinning attacks.

sections.heading: Anti-Pinning Policies
sections.content: Limits the size and shape of descendant transactions, allowing safe replace-by-fee (RBF) for multi-party protocols without the risk of an attacker making replacement prohibitively expensive.

nodes.label: Ephemeral Anchors
nodes.shortInfo: Allows 0-fee transactions with dust-value outputs to relay, provided they are spent by a fee-paying child.

sections.heading: Fee Sourcing Flexibility
sections.content: Relies on Package Relay and V3 Transactions. It eliminates the need for LN nodes to lock up capital in commitment transaction fees, allowing external fee sponsorship at the time of broadcast.

nodes.label: Ark Protocol
nodes.shortInfo: An off-chain protocol allowing users to share UTXOs and make cheap payments using Virtual UTXOs (VTXOs).

sections.heading: Scaling without Channels
sections.content: Ark spreads the cost of on-chain fees across multiple participants using trees of pre-signed transactions. It benefits greatly from covenant proposals like CTV.

nodes.label: Consensus Cleanup
nodes.shortInfo: A soft fork to fix legacy bugs: Time warp attack, slow-to-validate blocks, merkle tree weaknesses, and duplicate txids.

sections.heading: Technical Debt Reduction
sections.content: Addresses early design flaws from 2009, including placing limits on signature operations to prevent DoS attacks, and enforcing timing constraints to eliminate the time warp exploit.
